en.title: Shrek 2 Remaster Appears on Xbox Store, Aspyr Confirmed as Developer
en.summary: The beloved 2004 action-adventure game Shrek 2 is reportedly getting a modern remaster, with Aspyr Media at the helm. An Xbox Store listing has seemingly leaked details ahead of any official announcement.
en.body:
It appears that **Shrek 2: The Game**, the action-adventure title that accompanied the blockbuster animated film, is set to receive a modern remaster. Details have emerged via an unexpected Xbox Store listing, which names **Aspyr Media** as the developer behind the project. Aspyr, known for its recent work on ports and remasters of titles like *Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic* and *Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2*, seems to be bringing the ogre's second cinematic outing to current platforms.

While an official announcement has yet to materialize from Aspyr, Activision (the original publisher), or Microsoft, the listing has reportedly been verified by industry outlets like Push Square and GameSpot. The leaked information suggests the remaster will build upon the 2004 original, promising improved graphics and new features. Notably, the listing hints at the inclusion of up to four-player co-op, supporting both local and online multiplayer, a significant addition for fans who remember the original's multiplayer offerings.

## A Swampy Revival

The original **Shrek 2** video game launched in 2004, mirroring the film's massive success and offering players a chance to step into the swampy boots of Shrek, Donkey, and Puss in Boots. It was released across a variety of platforms, including the GameCube, PlayStation 2, Xbox, and PC, with a distinct version also available for the Game Boy Advance. The game itself was an action-adventure title, blending platforming, combat, and puzzle-solving elements as players journeyed through familiar locations from the movie.

The prospect of a remaster has certainly sparked interest among those who hold the original game dear. Fans have long cherished the humor and gameplay of the **Shrek 2** tie-in, and the potential for enhanced visuals and modern multiplayer features could introduce it to a new generation or offer a nostalgic trip for returning players. The inclusion of features like a photo mode and cheat mode, as suggested by the leak, further indicates a desire to cater to both dedicated fans and casual players looking for a fun, accessible experience.

## What’s Next for Far Far Away

While the Xbox Store listing has provided a tantalizing glimpse, official confirmation is still anticipated. Reports suggest that the **Shrek 2** remaster might be formally revealed at the upcoming ID@Xbox Showcase, with speculation pointing to October 20, 2026, as a potential reveal date. Until then, fans are left to ponder the full scope of this unexpected return to the world of Shrek, eagerly awaiting more details on platforms, release windows, and the full suite of features.
